findings.evidence: If the position counts as full-time, the stipend can apply. If the employee has completed 90 days of continuous service, the stipend can apply. If the request arrives before the benefit year ends, the stipend can apply. Only once every condition above is met does the home-office equipment stipend become available to the employee.
findings.fix: State the governing rule first, for example: The stipend applies only when all three conditions below are met, then list the three conditions.
findings.violation: The paragraph opens with three conditions, each phrased as if independently sufficient (the stipend can apply), before the fourth sentence reveals the governing rule that all three must hold together, so a reader has to reach the end and then re-read the opening three sentences to understand them correctly.

findings.evidence: 36-word sentence, 4 subordinate-clause markers: Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email.
findings.fix: Split the sentence at a subordinate-clause boundary.
findings.violation: The sentence runs to 36 words with 4 subordinate-clause markers, longer than the reader can hold in mind on a single pass.

findings.evidence: Program Overview: The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter ... Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time. Overview: The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time.
findings.fix: Delete one of the two Overview sections and state the publication cadence once, resolving which of the two statements is correct.
findings.violation: The document states the reimbursement log's publication cadence twice, under two near-identical headings, with two different and unreconciled answers, quarterly versus after every open enrollment period, so a reader who reads both cannot state which cadence is actually true.

findings.evidence: The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter. A copy of each update goes to the shared benefits folder the same day. Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the stipend budget each quarter. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time.
findings.fix: Keep one subject running through the paragraph, for example: The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter and sends a copy to the shared benefits folder the same day; staff can also request a printed copy at any time.
findings.violation: Each of the paragraph's four sentences opens on a new subject (the people operations office, a copy of each update, the IT asset group, staff) with no sentence picking up the subject the one before it established, so the reader has to re-orient at every sentence boundary instead of following one running topic.

findings.evidence: Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email.
findings.fix: Reorder so the sentence ends on the new, important fact, for example: because the assigned manager is traveling, the backup reviewer covering for them was never told this request needs their sign-off.
findings.violation: The sentence's newest, most important element, that the backup reviewer was never told sign-off is needed, lands in the middle of the sentence, and the sentence instead ends on the already-implied, lower-stakes detail that the portal releases a confirmation email, so the reader's attention lands on the least important part.

findings.evidence: The request is reviewed within two business days.
findings.fix: Rewrite the sentence in active voice, naming the actor that performs the action.
findings.violation: The sentence uses a be-verb plus past-participle passive construction in a context where the actor is recoverable and worth naming directly.

findings.evidence: Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email.
findings.fix: Move the staffing-delay note out of the reader-facing steps and into a short, clearly labeled aside, or state only what the reader needs: their request may take longer than two business days if the assigned reviewer is unavailable.
findings.violation: A how-to section written to the employee applicant shifts, in this one sentence, into internal staffing narrative about a manager and backup reviewer with no signal it is background rather than an instruction, leaving the reader unsure whether the sentence describes something they must do.

findings.evidence: Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time.
findings.fix: Replace the wordy phrase with its plain equivalent (for example, because for due to the fact that).
findings.violation: The sentence uses a wordy construction from the fixed wordy-phrase list that a shorter equivalent would carry with no loss of meaning.

findings.evidence: the reimbursement log (Program Overview); reimbursement is not available without a completed receipt (Eligibility); The stipend pays up to 500 dollars per benefit year ... the deposit happens in order to offset costs (Reimbursement Amounts)
findings.fix: Pick one term, for example stipend payment, and use it consistently for the payment itself, reserving reimbursement only for describing the process if that distinction matters.
findings.violation: Stipend, reimbursement, and deposit are used interchangeably for the same payment throughout the document with no defined-terms signal that they name one concept, so a careful reader can work out they are the same thing but has to check.

findings.evidence: However, reimbursement is not available without a completed receipt.
findings.fix: Restate the sentence with at most one negation, or recast it as a positive statement.
findings.violation: 2 negation markers from the fixed negation list co-occur in one clause, so the reader has to work out the statement's logical sign before understanding it.
